# openmetadata_glossary (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata glossary. Glossaries group glossary terms and can be marked mutually exclusive so a term can belong to only one of them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_glossary" "finance" {
  name               = "finance"
  display_name       = "Finance"
  description        = "Glossary owned by the finance data team."
  mutually_exclusive = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Glossary name. Changing it replaces the glossary, because the name is also its fully qualified name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Markdown description of the glossary.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.
- `mutually_exclusive` (Boolean) When true, a glossary term may belong to only one glossary under the same parent. The server fixes this at creation, so changing it replaces the glossary.

### Read-Only

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name. For a glossary this equals name.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_glossary.finance 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name, which for a glossary is its name.
terraform import openmetadata_glossary.finance finance
```
